name: Rickshaw Drone
description: A two-wheeled passenger cart pulled by a small ground drone or, in the cheapest versions, by a human runner. Common in the narrow streets of the Gray Zone and The Narrows where vehicles can't fit. The drone-pulled versions use repurposed delivery bots that were never designed for the weight and burn out every few months. The human-pulled versions are a reminder that some technologies go backward.
range: 5 km (drone battery), unlimited (human endurance, such as it is)
autonomy: Drone-pulled: semi-autonomous with route programming. Human-pulled: fully autonomous (the human kind).
common_usage: Short trips through narrow streets, elderly transport, tourist novelty in gentrified zones.
story_hooks: A rickshaw runner knows every back alley and hidden passage in the Gray Zone — they're the most valuable guide in the district
Drone rickshaws have started taking unauthorized detours through a district where something doesn't want to be seen
physical_description: A skeletal two-wheeled passenger cart welded from salvaged aluminum and rusted steel, its frame reinforced with duct tape and cable ties. The weathered passenger pod sits low between the wheels, its vinyl seat cracked and patched, with frayed safety straps hanging loose. The tow harness—either a mechanical coupling for burnt-out delivery drones or worn leather traces for human runners—trails forward into the perpetual rain-slicked streets.
